question.text: An NRI invests in an equity mutual fund in India. Upon redemption after 15 months with a long-term capital gain, what is the TDS obligation of the AMC?

answer.text: TDS at 12.5% on LTCG exceeding Rs. 1.25 lakh plus applicable surcharge and cess
No TDS for NRIs as they file returns in their country of residence
TDS at 10% as per the old LTCG rate for NRIs
TDS at 30% flat rate on all NRI mutual fund redemptions

explanation.text: The Logic: For an NRI investor in an equity-oriented mutual fund redeemed after the long-term holding period, the gain is taxed as equity LTCG under the Section 112A framework. The applicable LTCG rate on equity-oriented funds is 12.5% on the portion of gains exceeding the Rs. 1.25 lakh annual exemption, plus applicable surcharge and health & education cess. Unlike for resident investors where no TDS applies on capital gains, the AMC is required to deduct TDS on NRI redemption proceeds at the rate applicable to the type of gain. The Trap: Option B is wrong — TDS on capital gains is mandatory for NRIs regardless of where they file their returns. Option C uses the pre-revision 10% LTCG rate, which is outdated. Option D applies a flat 30% rate, which is incorrect for equity LTCG; the 30%/slab treatment applies to other categories of income, not equity LTCG. Note: The specific AMC TDS rule of 12.5% on equity LTCG above Rs. 1.25 lakh was not found in the cited workbook pages (V-A p.162 and X-B pp.242-244, 315-316). The V-A workbook acknowledges that NRI TDS is applicable and that rates depend on investor/investment/income type, and X-B supports Section 112A rates in general. The framing above reflects general industry/regulatory knowledge of NRI taxation under the current Income Tax Act.
